hooks.command: cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""'); deny() { printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}' "$1"; exit 0; }; case "$cmd" in git\ push*) echo "$cmd" | grep -qE 'origin main|origin/main' && deny 'No direct pushes to main — all changes must go via PRs'; branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none); [ "$branch" = "main" ] && ! echo "$cmd" | grep -qE 'origin [a-zA-Z]' && deny 'No direct pushes to main — all changes must go via PRs';; git\ commit*) echo "$cmd" | grep -qE 'APP-[0-9]+: ' || deny 'Commit message must start with APP-{N}: prefix (Linear issue required)'; branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main); [ "$branch" = "main" ] || echo "$branch" | grep -qE '^feat/app-[0-9]+-' || deny 'Branch name must match feat/app-{N}-* pattern (Linear issue required)';; git\ checkout\ -b\ *|git\ switch\ -c\ *) name=$(echo "$cmd" | sed -E 's/^git (checkout -b|switch -c) //; s/ .*//'); echo "$name" | grep -qE '^feat/app-[0-9]+-' || deny 'Branch name must match feat/app-{N}-* pattern (Linear issue required)';; git\ branch\ [a-zA-Z]*) name=$(echo "$cmd" | sed -E 's/^git branch //; s/ .*//'); echo "$name" | grep -qE '^feat/app-[0-9]+-' || deny 'Branch name must match feat/app-{N}-* pattern (Linear issue required)';; esac

hooks.prompt: Check if this Bash command is: (1) a git push to main — if it pushes directly to main (e.g. 'git push origin main', or 'git push' while on main branch), BLOCK it with 'No direct pushes to main — all changes must go via PRs'. (2) a git commit — verify the FULL command text contains 'APP-{N}: ' where N is a number (Linear issue reference) — note the commit message may span multiple lines in a heredoc. (3) creates a new branch (git checkout -b, git branch <name>, git switch -c) — verify the branch name matches 'feat/app-{N}-*' pattern. If the command is not related to git push/commit/branch creation, ALLOW it. If it violates a convention, BLOCK it with an explanation. Command: $ARGUMENTS
